items.title: Write the shared commit message rules
items.why: One rules file keeps the skill and the button consistent.
items.decisions: Format: '<Prefix>: <few-word summary>', prefix one of BC, New, Ref, Fix, Doc. Priority when mixed: BC, New, Fix, Ref, Doc. Doc only when no executable code changed. Details only when really necessary, one '- ' entry per line. No trailing period, no attribution lines, output only the message. Revision 1 replaces 'derive style from git log'.
items.acceptance: File exists, lists all five prefixes with meanings and the '- ' detail format, and is read by both the skill and the extension.
items.evidence: Created claude-plugin/skills/commit-message/commit-message-rules.md with format, five prefixes, priority order, BC rule, sources. Plugin-content test not yet written.

items.title: Add the commit-message skill with task context
items.why: The user wants a skill that proposes a commit message from the change and the task context, and never commits.
items.decisions: Interactive, user-invoked (disable-model-invocation: true). Reads the single .current marker, the task JSON name and description, and every *.md in the task folder; falls back to the diff alone without a unique marker. Excludes .history/ from the diff. Staged diff preferred, unstaged fallback. The diff decides content; reports give intent and type. Describes this change set, not the whole task. States nothing was committed.
items.acceptance: Frontmatter name equals folder name; skill states it does not commit; /vscode-workflow:commit-message prints a message in the required format and git log is unchanged.
items.evidence: Created claude-plugin/skills/commit-message/SKILL.md. test/claudePluginContent.test.ts checks: name equals folder name, disable-model-invocation is true, it reads the rules next to SKILL.md, the task JSON name and description, every *.md in the task folder, excludes .history, does not stage or commit, and does not read implementation-todo.json. The same rules gave a correctly formatted message in a live run through the generator.
items.remaining: Manual run of /vscode-workflow:commit-message in Claude Code after re-registering the plugin (Workflow: Register Agents and Skills with Claude Code, then /reload-plugins): it must print a message in the required format and leave git log unchanged.

items.title: Resolve the Claude CLI executable
items.why: claude is not always on PATH; the button must still work or fail clearly.
items.decisions: Order: setting claudePath, PATH, newest Claude Code extension binary. Pure, injectable lookup functions. Error names the setting.
items.acceptance: Unit tests cover the order, newest-version selection, and the missing-CLI error.
items.evidence: src/scm/claudeCli.ts plus src/scm/processRunner.ts. test/claudeCli.test.ts (7 tests) covers: configured path first, no fallback from a wrong configured path, PATH search, bundled binary, Windows claude.exe, missing-CLI error naming the setting, directory and non-executable files. test/processRunner.test.ts (8 tests) covers input, cwd, exit codes, missing program, abort, timeout. Full suite 164 tests pass. Design change: the bundled binary comes from the Claude Code extension's own path, not a folder scan.

items.title: Read the active task context for the prompt
items.why: Revision 1: the button must use the task name, description and reports, like the skill.
items.decisions: Locate the unique .current marker, read task name and description from the task JSON and every *.md in the task folder; cap each file and the total size; fall back to no context when there is no unique marker. Do not read implementation-todo.json.
items.acceptance: Unit tests cover no marker, two markers, caps, and the returned context text.
items.evidence: src/scm/taskContext.ts. test/taskContext.test.ts (6 tests) covers: name, description and Markdown reports in name order; implementation-todo.json and non-Markdown files ignored; no history, no active task, and two markers give undefined; malformed marker ignored; missing task file falls back to the marker name; per-report and total caps with omitted names; formatting. Suite passes.

items.title: Generate the message from the diff and task context
items.decisions: Staged diff with unstaged fallback; exclude .history/**, lock files and binaries from the diff; cap by maxDiffChars (default 60000); prompt built from the shared rules, task context and diff; headless CLI with no tools, no session persistence, no slash commands; abort and timeout; typed errors.
items.acceptance: Unit tests with a fake runner cover prompt, truncation, exclusions, CLI args, errors, and abort.
items.evidence: src/scm/commitMessageGenerator.ts. test/commitMessageGenerator.test.ts (26 tests): fake-runner unit tests for prompt, staged and unstaged scope, no task, pathspec exclusions, truncation with diff stat, model, untracked-only changes, NoChangesError, ClaudeRunError, abort pass-through, empty answer, argument list, cleanMessage, readMaxDiffChars; plus 5 functional tests with a real git repository and a fake claude program (stdin delivery, args, cwd, .history and lock files excluded, unstaged fallback, only-task-records case, failing program, not a repository). Found and fixed a real defect: outside a repository git diff failed with a confusing no-index message, so a rev-parse check now runs first. Live end-to-end run with the real claude 2.1.325 binary on this repository returned 'New: Add commit message generation' with three '- ' detail lines in about 2 seconds.
items.remaining: --setting-sources user still applies the user's own hooks and plugins; project and local settings are skipped.

items.title: Register the command and the Source Control menu
items.why: Gives the user the Generate Commit Message button in the Source Control input box.
items.decisions: Command vscode-workflow.generateCommitMessage on scm/inputBox; uses the passed SourceControl rootUri; progress with cancel; asks before replacing existing text; settings claudePath, maxDiffChars, model.
items.acceptance: Button appears and fills the box in the Extension Development Host; errors are clear; cancel works; existing text is never lost silently.
items.evidence: Created src/scm/commitMessageCommand.ts and src/scm/repositoryArgument.ts; registered in src/extension.ts; package.json has the command, the scm/inputBox menu entry (when scmProvider == git) and the settings claudePath, maxDiffChars, model. Typecheck passes.
items.remaining: Manual check in the Extension Development Host: the button, what VS Code passes to the scm/inputBox command (the code accepts a Uri or an object with rootUri and falls back to the Git API repositories), cancel, and the replace prompt. This cannot be run from this session.

items.title: Add and update tests
items.why: Protect the new plugin content and the new extension logic.
items.decisions: Add commit-message to the interactive skill list; assert the does-not-commit statement, the rules file, the five prefixes and the '- ' detail format; assert the skill reads the task JSON and reports and excludes .history/.
items.acceptance: npm run typecheck and npm test pass.
items.evidence: Added test/claudeCli.test.ts, test/taskContext.test.ts, test/commitMessageGenerator.test.ts, test/processRunner.test.ts, test/repositoryArgument.test.ts; updated test/claudePluginContent.test.ts (commit-message is a user-invoked skill; rules name all five prefixes and the '- ' format; skill reads rules, task JSON, reports, excludes .history, never commits) and test/tasksWebviewHtml.test.ts (Quick Reference). npm run typecheck passes and npm test passes: 15 files, 164 tests, run in the dev container. The esbuild bundle of src/extension.ts also builds.
items.remaining: No automated test covers commitMessageCommand.ts, which needs the VS Code API; it is checked manually (see the command item).

items.title: Update the documentation
items.why: The new skill, settings and button change user and maintainer behavior.
items.decisions: Fix the agent and skill counts; document the message format and five prefixes; document that the diff, task text and reports are sent to Claude; document the shared rules file.
items.acceptance: Docs match the implemented behavior and links resolve.
items.evidence: New docs/commit-messages.md (sources, format, prefixes, button, requirements, privacy, skill, troubleshooting), linked from docs/user-documentation.md. Updated docs/settings.md (three settings and the command), docs/skills-and-agents.md (commit-message section), docs/architecture.md (src/scm layout and a keep-in-sync note on the shared rules file and the CLI flags), and the Quick Reference panel in src/tasks/tasksWebviewHtml.ts. README.md needs no change: it lists only the two index pages.
